metadata.note: The Fort Smith and Western, Fort Smith AR - Coal Creek (over the KCS) - McCurtain - Crowder - Okemah - Prague - Fallis OK, then Fallis - Guthrie (own, to 1915) and Fallis - Oklahoma City (over the Katy, from Dec 1915). It never touched Poteau, Wilburton or McAlester. Four FS&W features (one per drawable span), plus the affiliated St. Louis, El Reno and Western (Guthrie - El Reno) as its own company and colour. Not drawn: 1902-03 partial operation before the through opening (no passenger evidence); the Joplin - Oklahoma City MO&G through sleeper (covered by the FS&W features; MO&G's part belongs to its own layer); coal-mine spurs near McCurtain/Bokoshe; and the post-1939 Fort Smith and Van Buren Railway (KCS), Coal Creek - West Panther, freight only (Rule 1).
sources: research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt (KCS section, Table 7: FS&VB freight service only)
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing trimmed: drawn from scratch. The FS&VB (KCS) Coal Creek - West Panther, 1939-1990s, freight only per the Feb 1952 Official Guide, is deliberately not drawn, and fsw-coal-creek-fallis ends at 1938, not at the 1939 shutdown, the Aug 1939 abandonment, the 1992 KCS merger or the 1994 abandonment filing.
not_yet_sourced: fsw-fort-smith-coal-creek, fsw-coal-creek-fallis, fsw-fallis-guthrie START [OPEN]: 1905 is the earliest Official Guide listing seen; the line opened through Nov 1, 1903 and 1903 is very likely. 1902-03 partial operation (ICC 'operated from Feb 1, 1902') has no passenger evidence.
fsw-fort-smith-coal-creek END [OPEN]: confirmed to April 1932 (Fort Smith - Oklahoma City sleeper). 1933-1938 very probable but no source names Fort Smith.

fsw-fallis-guthrie END [OPEN]: confirmed to 1914 (Fowler, 1914 company timetable). Service after the Dec 1915 Oklahoma City re-route, and the stub's abandonment date, unknown. Bryant, 'Railroad Redundant: The Fort Smith & Western Railway', Railroad History 174 (1996), and George & Wood, The Railroads of Oklahoma (R&LHS Bulletin 60, 1943) are the likely sources; neither was seen.

fsw-coal-creek-fallis / fsw-fallis-oklahoma-city END 1938: last positive passenger statement (June-Sept 1938 restoration; Aug 28, 1938 OKC photo). Whether mixed trains carried passengers Sept 1938 - Jan/Feb 1939 is unsourced. Shutdown date conflict: Jan 19, 1939 (Condren) vs Feb 9, 1939 (Wikipedia).

slerw-guthrie-el-reno [ANCHOR] 1905 only. Opening (June 1904?) and end (1923/1924/1925 conflict) unconfirmed; who operated it (SLER&W or FS&W) unresolved. El Reno papers on gateway.okhistory.org (1903-05) not searched.
Junction point of the Joplin - Oklahoma City MO&G through sleeper (Dustin or Weleetka?) not established.
All headway_min (720) and avg_speed_kmh (30) values are estimates.

Station sites: FS&W Fort Smith stations, Katy Oklahoma City station and SLER&W El Reno station are not drawn to; McCurtain - Crowder (43 mi) and Richland - El Reno (10 mi) are straight-line approximations.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap via its Overpass API, traced with opstrace.py. old_railway_operator probe ~FS.?&.?W|Fort Smith over Oklahoma/Arkansas found one way (166023878, Coal Creek - Bokoshe). OHM ways named 'Fort Smith and Western Railway' (198738921, 199978245) carry Crowder - Fallis - Meridian; OHM 'Katy' way 198738933 carries Fallis - Oklahoma City; KCS-tagged OSM ways carry Fort Smith - Coal Creek.

properties.line: Fort Smith and Western: Fort Smith – Coal Creek (KCS trackage)
properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced: no FS&W running time was found; ~30 km/h assumed for a lightly built steam road that ran mixed trains from 1932 (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overpass, traced with opstrace.py on the Kansas City Southern: the abandoned KCS Fort Smith - Spiro grade (old_railway_operator=KCS, ways 165858893, 165858857, 165858891; lifted after the May 1943 flood) and the live KCS Heavener Subdivision from Spiro to Coal Creek (ways 1025910987, 915840090 ...).
properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg: 19.2 mi drawn against 19.3 mi of KCS trackage rights (ICC valuation vol. 134) + 1.0 mi of FS&W-owned Fort Smith terminal; Fowler gives Fort Smith 0.0 - Coal Creek 20.1. Every mile is on KCS-tagged ways (the route is deliberately the KCS, which FS&W trains used under trackage rights). Fort Smith end: drawn to the north end of the OSM KCS abandoned grade (about 35.368 N, 94.433 W), roughly 2.3 km short of downtown; the FS&W's own 1.0 mi terminal to its station at 10th and Garrison (relocated 1932 to South A and South 11th Streets) is NOT drawn. ALIGNMENT: the Spiro - Coal Creek part is today's KCS Heavener Subdivision; any realignment since 1905-32 was not checked.

segments.note: FS&W passenger trains over the Kansas City Southern from Fort Smith (FS&W station, 10th and Garrison; new brick depot at South A and South 11th Streets in 1932) via Peno and Spiro to Coal Creek ('Fort Smith & Western Junction'), under trackage rights: the FS&W paid the KCS $400/mi/yr plus 50% of local passenger fares between Coal Creek and Fort Smith (ICC Valuation vol. 134), so FS&W passenger trains demonstrably ran here. The company is drawn as the FS&W because it was the FS&W's trains; the track and geometry belong to the KCS, which ran its own Fort Smith passenger trains until Aug 31, 1941 (Condren). Fort Smith - Guthrie Pullman sleeper Jan 18, 1906 - Feb 3, 1907; Fort Smith - Oklahoma City vestibule sleeper from Dec 1915, carried on mixed trains by April 1932 (Condren). [OPEN] START: 1905 is the earliest CONFIRMED passenger year (FS&W station names in the 1905 Official Guide, per Fowler's Oklahoma list), not a known start. The line opened through Fort Smith - Guthrie on Nov 1, 1903 (Wikipedia) and 1903 is very likely, but no source seen names a passenger train before 1905. Do not move earlier without evidence. [OPEN] END: 1932 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - the Fort Smith - Oklahoma City sleeper is confirmed 'to at least April 1932'. FS&W trains very probably kept reaching Fort Smith (it kept its 1932 depot) until operations ceased Jan 19 or Feb 9, 1939 (source conflict), and 1933-1938 is very probably real, but no source seen names Fort Smith for those years. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 720 min (about two trains each way a day) is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: ICC Valuation vol. 134 (KCS trackage rights, fare split); Condren Rails FS&W passenger-train history (1906-07 Fort Smith - Guthrie sleeper; Fort Smith - Oklahoma City sleeper Dec 1915 to at least April 1932); Fowler's Oklahoma list line 80 (1905 Official Guide station names). Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Fort Smith and Western: Main Line (Coal Creek – Fallis)
properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced: no FS&W running time was found; ~30 km/h assumed for a lightly built steam road that ran mixed trains from 1932 (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: Coal Creek - Bokoshe: OSM way 166023878 (abandoned, old_railway_operator=FS&W). Bokoshe - east of McCurtain: OSM abandoned ways 14839117 and 14839124 (named 'Kansas City Southern Railway': the FS&W grade that the KCS-controlled Fort Smith and Van Buren Railway kept for freight after 1939). Crowder - Fallis: OpenHistoricalMap ways 198738921 and 199978245 ('Fort Smith and Western Railway', 1899-1939-02-01). Traced with opstrace.py; McCurtain - Crowder is a chain of straight lines through geocoded town centres.
properties.geometry_quality: Partly approximated: 172.1 mi drawn against Fowler's 174.9 mi (Coal Creek MP 20.1 to Fallis MP 195.0; ICC: Coal Creek - McCurtain 17.70 mi + McCurtain - S. Canadian River 59.0 + S. Canadian River - Lincoln County 69.0 + ~30 mi of the Lincoln County - Guthrie stage). TRACED: Coal Creek - grade end east of McCurtain 15.5 mi on OSM abandoned FS&W/FS&VB grade; Crowder - Fallis 110.9 mi on the OHM FS&W ways (Fowler 83.0 to 195.0 = 112.0 mi; waypoint fit Indianola 0.8 km, Hanna 0.2, Dustin 0.1, Weleetka 0.5, Okemah 0.4, Boley 0.4, Prague 0.4, Wellston 0.8, Fallis 1.1 km). STRAIGHT LINES, 45.7 mi in all (no surviving grade in OSM or OHM between McCurtain and Crowder): grade end E of McCurtain - McCurtain 2.4 mi; McCurtain - Panther 2.0 mi; Panther - Lequire 6.5 mi; Lequire - Kinta 7.4 mi; Kinta - Quinton 7.2 mi; Quinton - Featherston 7.7 mi; Featherston - Blocker 4.6 mi; Blocker - Crowder (OHM grade start) 7.9 mi. Fowler gives McCurtain 38.0 - Crowder 83.0 = 45.0 mi, so the chain runs about 1.7 mi short of the real curving line up the Sans Bois valley; town-centre geocodes (Panther, Lequire, Featherston, Blocker are hamlets) stand in for station sites. The Crowder end of the OHM grade is 1.0 km from Crowder town. ALIGNMENT: the OSM/OHM grades are the only ones recorded for this road (lifted 1939-40 west of McCurtain) and are taken to be the 1903-38 alignment; the Bokoshe - McCurtain ways are the FS&VB-era (post-1939) form of the same grade and were not checked against a pre-1939 map.

segments.note: Fort Smith and Western Railroad main line, Coal Creek - Bokoshe - McCurtain - Kinta - Quinton - Crowder (Katy crossing) - Hanna - Dustin - Weleetka - Okemah - Boley - Paden - Prague - Wellston - Fallis, with through trains continuing to Guthrie (see fsw-fallis-guthrie). Coal Creek - McCurtain built 1901 for the San Bois coal leases; through Fort Smith - Guthrie opening Nov 1, 1903 (Wikipedia). Fort Smith - Guthrie Pullman sleeper Jan 18, 1906 - Feb 3, 1907; no sleeping cars Feb 1907 - Dec 1915 (Condren). Receivership from Oct 1915 did not change who ran the trains. [OPEN] START: 1905 is the earliest CONFIRMED passenger year (FS&W station names in the 1905 Official Guide, per Fowler's Oklahoma list), not a known start. The line opened through Fort Smith - Guthrie on Nov 1, 1903 (Wikipedia) and 1903 is very likely, but no source seen names a passenger train before 1905. Do not move earlier without evidence. Headway 720 min (about two trains each way a day) is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia FS&W article (Nov 1, 1903 through opening); Fowler's Oklahoma list line 80 (1905 Official Guide station names, mileposts); Condren Rails FS&W passenger-train history (1906-07 sleeper); ICC Valuation vol. 134 (construction stages). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: From Dec 1915 through trains were re-routed from Guthrie to Oklahoma City over the Katy from Fallis (see fsw-fallis-oklahoma-city): a Fort Smith - Oklahoma City vestibule sleeper, a Joplin - Oklahoma City joint sleeper with the Missouri, Oklahoma and Gulf (Dec 1915 to at least June 1916, possibly into 1917), and in May 1916 'a handsome five-coach vestibuled train, with sleepers and buffet cars' (Condren). Cafe service had ended before Jan 1928. Company renamed Fort Smith and Western Railway 1921 (Condren) / left receivership Feb 1, 1923 (Wikipedia) - same company throughout. Headway 720 min (about two trains each way a day) is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: Condren Rails FS&W passenger-train history (Dec 1915 re-route and sleepers, May 1916 train, cafe service ended before Jan 1928, sleeper to at least April 1932); ICC Valuation vol. 134 (MKT trackage rights from Dec 6, 1915). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: By April 1932 the passenger trains had become MIXED trains, still carrying the Fort Smith - Oklahoma City sleeper; by Feb 1933 the sleepers were gone; around June 13, 1938 the mixed trains were briefly replaced by passenger trains for about three months (Condren). Mixed trains count as passenger service (CLAUDE.md Rule 1). Fowler cites the 1933 Official Guide for the station name 'South Canadian'. Second receivership from June 1, 1931. END 1938: the last year with a positive passenger statement. Operations ceased Jan 19, 1939 (Condren timeline) or Feb 9, 1939 (Wikipedia) - SOURCE CONFLICT, unresolved; mixed trains in Jan 1939 are plausible but not sourced, so the line is not drawn into 1939, and the Aug 1939 abandonment is not an end year. Afterwards Coal Creek - McCurtain/West Panther (~20 mi) became the KCS's Fort Smith and Van Buren Railway, freight only (Official Guide Feb 1952, KCS Table 7) - not drawn (Rule 1); the rest was lifted 1939-40. 1933-1938 rests on one secondary source (Condren). Headway 720 min (about two trains each way a day) is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: Condren Rails FS&W passenger-train history (mixed trains by April 1932, no sleepers by Feb 1933, passenger trains restored ~June 13, 1938 for ~3 months); Condren timeline and Wikipedia (Jan 19 vs Feb 9, 1939 shutdown); Fowler line 80 (1933 Official Guide station name). Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Fort Smith and Western: Fallis – Guthrie
properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced: no FS&W running time was found; ~30 km/h assumed for a lightly built steam road that ran mixed trains from 1932 (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap way 199978245 ('Fort Smith and Western Railway', 1899-1939-02-01) Fallis - Meridian; OSM abandoned ways 534164473, 534164472, 534161901 (no operator tag) Meridian - Guthrie. Traced with opstrace.py.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg: 23.3 mi drawn against 22.0 mi documented (Fowler line 81, Fallis 195.0 - Guthrie 217.0). Fallis - Meridian (9.6 mi) is on the OHM FS&W way; Meridian - Guthrie (12.9 mi) is on untagged OSM abandoned ways that continue the OHM FS&W grade westward (OHM has an untagged way 198738850 on the same corridor). The Santa Fe's Eastern Oklahoma Railway (Guthrie - Chandler) approached Guthrie from the east nearby, so the last few miles into Guthrie may in part draw that road's grade rather than the FS&W's - not checked. Guthrie end: drawn to about 35.872 N, 97.426 W near the AT&SF station that the FS&W used under a joint-facility agreement (ICC). ALIGNMENT not checked against a 1903-14 map.

segments.note: The original western end of the FS&W main line, Fallis - Shiloh - Meridian - Irving - Guthrie (AT&SF station, joint facility), built 1903 by the Fort Smith and Western Railroad of Oklahoma and bought into the Arkansas company. Guthrie was the territorial capital when it was built; the capital moved to Oklahoma City in 1910 and the FS&W re-routed its through trains there over the Katy in Dec 1915. Fort Smith - Guthrie Pullman sleeper Jan 18, 1906 - Feb 3, 1907 (Condren). [OPEN] START: 1905 is the earliest CONFIRMED passenger year (FS&W station names in the 1905 Official Guide, per Fowler's Oklahoma list), not a known start. The line opened through Fort Smith - Guthrie on Nov 1, 1903 (Wikipedia) and 1903 is very likely, but no source seen names a passenger train before 1905. Do not move earlier without evidence. [OPEN] END: 1914 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - Fowler's FS&W legend 'a: 1914t' (1914 company timetable) lists Irving on this stub. Through service very probably ran to Dec 1915 and a local or mixed train may have served Guthrie later, perhaps to 1939; nothing found dates it. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 720 min (about two trains each way a day) is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler's Oklahoma list line 81 (legend a: 1914t, 1914 company timetable); Condren Rails (Fort Smith - Guthrie sleeper 1906-07); ICC Valuation vol. 134 (AT&SF Guthrie joint facility). Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Fort Smith and Western: Fallis – Oklahoma City (Katy trackage)
properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced: no FS&W running time was found; ~30 km/h assumed for a lightly built steam road that ran mixed trains from 1932 (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap way 198738933 ('Katy', 1904-1973), the Missouri-Kansas-Texas Oklahoma City line, traced with opstrace.py (waypoints Fallis, Luther, Arcadia). A 0.6 mi connector joins it to the FS&W at Fallis, where the two OHM ways do not meet.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg except a 0.6 mi junction connector at Fallis (the OHM FS&W and Katy ways pass 0.8 km apart and never join): 31.2 mi drawn against 32.49 mi of MKT trackage rights plus Oklahoma City terminals (ICC) and Fowler's 32.9 mi (195.0 - 227.9). The OHM Katy way runs via Luther (1.2 km) and Arcadia (0.6 km), NOT via Jones (Jones and the parallel live 'SLWC Sooner Subdivision' are the Frisco line, deliberately avoided). Oklahoma City end: drawn to the end of the OHM Katy way at about 35.470 N, 97.468 W, about 4 km east-northeast of downtown; the last ~1-2 mi into the Katy passenger station are NOT drawn and the station site was not established. The OHM way is a coarse hand-drawn line, not a surveyed grade. ALIGNMENT not checked against a 1915-38 map.

segments.note: FS&W passenger trains over the Missouri-Kansas-Texas ('Katy') from Fallis via Luther and Arcadia to the Katy station in Oklahoma City, under a trackage-rights agreement dated Dec 6, 1915 (ICC Valuation vol. 134; rent $22,500/yr for the line and $7,500/yr for terminals plus 60% of certain local revenue). Drawn as an FS&W feature because these were FS&W trains; the track belongs to the Katy, which ran its own trains here. Fort Smith - Oklahoma City vestibule sleeper and Joplin - Oklahoma City joint sleeper with the MO&G from Dec 1915; sleeper confirmed to at least April 1932, by then on mixed trains (Condren). 1933-1938 is medium confidence: it rests on Condren's photo caption of an FS&W locomotive at the Oklahoma City Katy station on Aug 28, 1938 'near the end of service of the railroad in Oklahoma City', during the June-September 1938 passenger-train restoration. The MKT withdrew the trackage rights in Jan 1939 for unpaid rent (Wikipedia). If only route-explicit evidence is accepted, the confirmed span is 1915-1932. Headway 720 min (about two trains each way a day) is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: ICC Valuation vol. 134 (MKT trackage rights from Dec 6, 1915); Condren Rails (Dec 1915 sleepers, sleeper to at least April 1932, Aug 28, 1938 OKC Katy station photo caption); Wikipedia (MKT withdrew rights Jan 1939). Headway not sourced.

properties.company: St. Louis, El Reno and Western Railway
properties.line: St. Louis, El Reno and Western: Guthrie – El Reno
properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced: no SLER&W running time was found (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap way 198739647 (railway, no name; start_date 1851 'arbitrary'), the only grade recorded between Guthrie and Piedmont, traced with opstrace.py; Richland - El Reno is a straight line.
properties.geometry_quality: Partly approximated: 40.6 mi drawn against 42.0 mi documented (Fowler line 101; Encyclopedia of Oklahoma History; Wikipedia). TRACED: Guthrie - near Richland 30.9 mi on OHM way 198739647, which carries no name or operator - it is taken to be the SLER&W because it is the only railway Guthrie - Piedmont (Piedmont 0.1 km, Richland 0.2 km from it) and no other road ran that way, but the attribution is inferred, not tagged. STRAIGHT LINE: Richland - El Reno 9.7 mi (no grade in OSM or OHM; it crosses the North Canadian River valley, where the bridge condemned after a 1920 flood stood). El Reno end: town-centre geocode, not the SLER&W station site. The 0.6 mi over the AT&SF from Guthrie to El Reno Junction is within the drawn Guthrie end. ALIGNMENT not checked against a 1905 map.

segments.note: St. Louis, El Reno and Western Railway, Guthrie - El Reno Junction (0.6 mi over the AT&SF) - Dutcher/Lookout - Navina - Lockridge - Piedmont - Richland - Smithton - El Reno, 42 mi. A separate company, 51% of its stock owned by the Fort Smith and Western (ICC Valuation vol. 134, 1918 data), so it takes its own company and colour: who actually ran its trains (SLER&W crews or FS&W) was not established, and Wikipedia's SLER&W article says it was 'merged into' the FS&W, contradicting the ICC - SOURCE CONFLICT, unresolved. [ANCHOR]: 1905 is the ONLY confirmed passenger year (every station listed in the 1905 Official Guide, Fowler legend 'a: 1905G'). Service certainly ran wider both ways - Wikipedia says it began operating June 1904 (a Feb 1904 El Reno paper reportedly called it complete), and it ran into the 1910s - but no other year is confirmed. The end is unknown: Wikipedia says the Canadian River bridge was condemned after a 1920 flood, service 'sputtered' to 1923, ran briefly in 1925 [citation needed] and ended late 1925; the Encyclopedia of Oklahoma History says it was abandoned in 1924. Do not widen this anchor without a dated timetable or a 'last train' story. Headway 720 min is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler's Oklahoma list line 101 (legend a: 1905G, all stations in the 1905 Official Guide); ICC Valuation vol. 134 (51% FS&W stock ownership); Wikipedia SLER&W article and Encyclopedia of Oklahoma History (conflicting end dates, not drawn). Headway not sourced.
